organization.name: Gani Georgiev / PocketBase
organization.notes: Individual volunteer project, explicitly neither startup nor business. Creator says work began late2021; public release followed July2022. Equity financing not applicable; past donations and possible grants are distinct. No paid company or investor roster.

pricingTiers.name: PocketBase open source
pricingTiers.notes: Standalone open-source binary/framework; infrastructure separate; no vendor hosting.
No explicit Most popular or Recommended plan designation verified in the pricing source; no plan inferred.
Personal volunteer project explicitly has no paid team/company; no organizational license plan published.
No paid enterprise plan; FAQ states no paid company and no support commitment.

moats.claim: A compact SQLite-backed architecture and extensible API attract lightweight applications; defensibility is limited by permissive source access and a deliberately narrow single-server scope.

productReasons.claim: Manage SQLite collections, validation, REST endpoints and realtime subscriptions from an integrated schema dashboard.
Add password/OAuth user authentication and attach files with on-demand image thumbnails to records.
Extend routes and event hooks in embedded JavaScript or compile custom Go application logic.

sponsorship.notes: Checked official FAQ donation/sponsorship statement: individual donations no longer accepted; organizational no-strings grants invited. No named corporate sponsor disclosed there; personal steward is not a business fallback.

requirements.notes: Native standalone binary; persistent pb_data directory.
Embedded; MySQL/MariaDB/PostgreSQL not supported out of box.
Highly recommended; Unix sendmail default unsuitable for reliable delivery.
Files/backups local default; backups can use separate S3 bucket.
Built-in HTTPS available; custom Docker image possible, no official image.
Built into binary; Node.js not required.

requirements.condition: Build custom application as Go framework
requirements.notes: Build time only; default pure-Go SQLite needs no CGO.

resources.notes: No minimum hardware published. FAQ2vCPU/4GB example is a benchmark, not minimum; storage scales with data.

selfHosting.notes: Single-server backend; no external SQL,Redis,queue or separate runtime service required. Documentation warns pre1.0 compatibility/migrations can change.

oneClickInstall.notes: Official docs offer binary download and manual server/Dockerfile recipes; no maintained one-click, marketplace or installer command verified. Running an already downloaded binary is not an installer.
